problem: Saying the preheader "runs exactly once" is too strong. A preheader runs once each time the loop is entered. If the loop sits inside an outer loop, or the routine containing it is called many times, the preheader runs many times. As written, a student may think hoisting to the preheader always means one execution in the whole program.
fix: A block placed on the edge(s) entering the loop header, so it becomes the only outside predecessor. It runs exactly once per entry to the loop, so an invariant computed there is evaluated once per loop execution instead of once per iteration, without changing the loop body's control flow.

problem: The C program is introduced as the transformed loop that stores a constant into every fourth element of A, but the code never performs A[t1] = t2. It only accumulates sum and n. The printed output is right, but the code does not match the stated transformed loop, so a student comparing step 7 with the listing sees a mismatch.
fix: Either add the store, e.g. int A[400]; ... while (t1 <= 396) { A[t1] = t2; sum += t2; n++; t1 += 4; }, or state that the listing only counts iterations and totals the stored values and omits the array for brevity.
